items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: I just didn’t want to be this Glen Howard guy who played the hell out of Rachmaninoff.

ctx.x: You know I learned how to improvise blues before I learned how to play the trombone you know. I was just playing stuff that was in my head you know. And then I found out when I got in my father’s band I had to read music and I had to learn how to play the trombone you know. So I learned what I had to learn after I learned how to improvise.

Did spending time at the piano help with the improvising? Because I know, I read in your book that you had the typical sort of classical lessons, but, I actually have a quote here. You wrote: “ I just didn’t want to be this Glen Howard guy who played the hell out of Rachmaninoff. I wanted to play the shit out of the trombone solo in “Things Ain’t What They Used to Be.”

Yeah, yeah. Well you know Gwen Howard was a girl. And I didn’t want to play that nice little dainty music like girls played you know. I wanted to play like “Things Ain’t What It Used to Be.” So that was in my head you know. I can play the boogie woogie on the piano with my left hand and in my right hand I played the chord. I didn’t know what I was doing but I was hearing it in my head you know. So that’s what I learned before I learned music. You know? I knew how to play, how to improvise and how to make up music…
